title: Verifiable ad delivery and influencer metrics
problem: Ad networks report impressions and clicks using their own unauditable metrics, enabling widespread fraud. Brands also pay influencers based on self-reported or platform-reported reach and engagement that is trivially inflated through bots and fake followers.
solutionSketch: Transparent impression tracking and verifiable reach metrics — with optional zero-knowledge proofs for audience size — so advertisers can independently confirm that spend reached real human audiences.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: delivery events and engagement signals can be cryptographically attested — giving advertisers independent proof that their spend reached real audiences without relying on the platform's own reporting.

title: Affordable housing covenant enforcement
problem: Affordable housing deed restrictions — requiring units to remain below market rate for 30, 50, or 99 years — are written into paper legal documents that must be manually checked at every ownership transfer, and routinely slip through conveyancing processes, effectively converting affordable units to market rate with no enforcement mechanism.
solutionSketch: Affordability restrictions encoded directly into property tokens that enforce covenants automatically at the point of transfer or rental — making it structurally impossible to sell or rent above the allowed price without the covenant being triggered.
whyEthereum: Enforcement: affordability rules are baked into the asset itself and execute at every transfer — covenant compliance becomes a property of the token, not a legal obligation that requires someone to notice and litigate a violation.

title: Age and eligibility proofs without identity disclosure
problem: A teenager trying to prove they're 18 to access a website, or a doctor proving they hold a medical license to prescribe remotely, must hand over their full government ID — exposing date of birth, address, and ID number to a third party who only needed a yes/no answer — creating surveillance infrastructure and breach risk for a simple eligibility check.
solutionSketch: Zero-knowledge proofs that let individuals demonstrate they meet a threshold — over 18, licensed physician, accredited investor — without revealing the underlying document, name, or any other personal attribute beyond the specific claim being verified.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: zero-knowledge proofs confirm eligibility cryptographically without exposing underlying identity — platforms get regulatory compliance without building a database of sensitive documents that becomes a breach target.

title: Agent-to-agent commerce protocols
problem: As specialized AI agents proliferate — managing calendars, researching suppliers, executing purchases — they need to hire, pay, and contract with each other autonomously. There is no open protocol for agents to discover services, agree terms, and settle payments without routing every transaction through a human approval loop.
solutionSketch: Open protocols for AI agents to publish capabilities, negotiate service terms, execute purchases, and settle micropayments autonomously — creating a machine-to-machine service economy where agents from any organization can transact as fluidly as APIs call each other today.
whyEthereum: Composability: a shared settlement layer with open standards lets agents from any organization transact without pre-negotiated bilateral integrations — the agent economy becomes interoperable by default rather than requiring every agent developer to build custom payment bridges.

title: Economic identity for agents and devices
problem: Autonomous AI agents and IoT devices interact with services and execute transactions but have no standardized identity, wallet, or payment rails — making it impossible to attribute actions, manage permissions, hold assets, or enable machine-scale micropayments without routing every transaction through human-operated intermediaries. solutionSketch: Onchain identity and payment rails purpose-built for autonomous agents and devices — enabling them to hold funds, pay for services, sign transactions, transfer ownership, and build verifiable track records across platforms without human approval loops or centralized registries.
whyEthereum: Enforcement: smart contracts can scope an agent's permissions and spending limits programmatically, and Ethereum's global settlement layer means an agent's identity and funds work across any application without custom integrations.

title: Tamper-evident maintenance records for aviation MRO
problem: Airlines and MRO providers maintain aircraft maintenance records across disconnected paper logbooks and legacy systems, making FAA/EASA audit preparation weeks of manual work and leaving no reliable way to detect falsified inspection signoffs — a safety failure that has contributed to multiple airworthiness directives and enforcement actions.
solutionSketch: Immutable, per-component maintenance logs that record every inspection, part replacement, and airworthiness directive compliance event — giving regulators a continuous, tamper-evident audit trail rather than sampling paper records during periodic inspections.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: each maintenance event is cryptographically attested at the time it occurs — falsified inspections become detectable after the fact, and audit preparation collapses from weeks to hours because the regulator reads the same ledger the MRO writes to.

title: Business registries and beneficial ownership
problem: Verifying a company's registration, licensing status, or true ownership requires navigating multiple disconnected databases — and existing beneficial ownership registries rely on self-reported filings with no verification mechanism, allowing shell company structures to hide the real owners of assets across jurisdictions. solutionSketch: Cryptographically attested business registration and beneficial ownership records that chain legal entities to verified ultimate owners across jurisdictions — enabling instant verification for regulators, banks, and counterparties without relying on self-filed declarations or bilateral data-sharing between registries.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: ownership attestations are cryptographically signed and immutable across jurisdictions — false filings become detectable and cross-border verification happens on a shared neutral ledger rather than through slow bilateral regulatory cooperation.

title: Shared-ledger bookkeeping with counterparty confirmation
problem: Intercompany transactions and multi-entity consolidation require each party to independently record and reconcile the same economic event — a process that consumes 30-40% of the time in monthly close cycles and makes audit preparation expensive because auditors must independently confirm balances with counterparties through a manual confirmation process that takes weeks.
solutionSketch: A shared ledger where both counterparties to a transaction confirm the same record at the point of origination — eliminating the reconciliation step during close and giving auditors real-time access to pre-confirmed balances rather than requiring them to send confirmation letters and wait for responses.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: every transaction is confirmed by both counterparties at origination on a shared, tamper-evident ledger — the monthly reconciliation step that drives close cycle length and audit cost is eliminated by construction.

problem: Community land trusts and housing cooperatives are structured as 501(c)(3)s or limited equity co-ops with governance rules buried in paper bylaws that members rarely read, share transfers processed through manual legal work, and financial reporting that requires expensive annual audits — overhead that scales linearly with the number of units and makes it prohibitively expensive to operate community-owned housing at anything beyond neighborhood scale.

title: Privacy-preserving KYC and sanctions screening proofs
problem: Every financial institution that onboards the same customer independently collects and stores the same identity documents, running redundant KYC checks that cost $50–500 per customer — while creating dozens of copies of sensitive identity data across institutions that each become breach targets. Cross-border transactions compound the problem: a European bank processing a payment to a US correspondent must demonstrate OFAC and EU sanctions compliance, which currently requires sharing enough customer data for the counterparty to independently screen — forcing a choice between privacy and compliance.
solutionSketch: Zero-knowledge proofs that let institutions demonstrate a customer passed KYC and sanctions screening — proving the fact of compliance without sharing the underlying identity documents, so counterparties can satisfy their regulatory obligations without receiving (and storing) sensitive data they didn't need.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: ZK proofs confirm compliance status cryptographically — counterparties verify that screening was performed without receiving the underlying identity data, reducing breach surface while satisfying correspondent banking compliance requirements.

title: Automated agricultural subsidy disbursement
problem: Agricultural subsidy programs (e.g., EU Common Agricultural Policy direct payments, USDA conservation programs) require farmers to submit annual applications, undergo eligibility reviews, and wait months for payment — a process where administrative overhead consumes a significant share of program budgets and delays reach the farmers who need operating capital most. solutionSketch: Subsidy disbursements that execute automatically when satellite-verified acreage data, crop identification, and conservation practice adoption confirm eligibility — reducing administrative costs and getting payments to farmers at the start of the season rather than months after application.
whyEthereum: Enforcement: payments release automatically when oracle-verified eligibility conditions are confirmed — farmers receive funds when they need operating capital rather than after months of manual review, and the eligibility check is continuous rather than sampled.

title: Content provenance and authenticity
problem: There is no widespread mechanism to verify who created a post, photo, video, or article — making impersonation trivial and deepfake attribution impossible to contest. The problem compounds with AI: AI-generated content is indistinguishable from human-created content once shared, and users receiving AI outputs have no way to verify which model produced a given result, enabling manipulation and undermining accountability for both human and AI-generated misinformation.
solutionSketch: Signed posts, media receipts, and provenance chains that cover both human-created and AI-generated content — cryptographically binding content to its origin at creation time, so that deepfakes, impersonation, and model-version manipulation are publicly detectable.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: cryptographic signatures attached at creation time prove who made content and when — impersonation and retroactive denial become publicly detectable rather than just deniable.

title: Credit scoring from verified off-chain financial history
problem: Hundreds of millions of people are creditworthy — they pay rent on time, maintain savings, and run profitable small businesses — but are invisible to formal lenders because their financial history lives in bank apps, rental platforms, and payroll systems that lenders can't access without the borrower surrendering raw account credentials.

problem: Insurance companies face hundreds of disputed claims monthly that don't fit automated processing rules — ambiguous coverage questions, contested damage assessments, conflicting evidence — and route them through traditional arbitration that takes 7–10 days, costs hundreds of dollars per case, and produces outcomes neither party finds credible.

whyEthereum: Enforcement: adjudication outcomes execute automatically via smart contract — neither the insurer nor the claimant can delay compliance with a verdict, and the juror incentive structure is enforced programmatically rather than by a professional arbitration body.

title: Tamper-evident data integrity for decentralized clinical trials

FDA's 2023 DCT guidance specifically calls out electronic source data integrity as a key concern.
solutionSketch: Cryptographic attestation of clinical trial data at the point of collection — patient-reported outcomes, wearable sensor readings, and eConsent signatures are hashed and timestamped on an immutable ledger at the moment of capture, creating an audit trail that satisfies 21 CFR Part 11 requirements and gives monitors, sponsors, and regulators confidence in source data integrity without requiring physical site visits.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: trial data is cryptographically committed at the point of collection — monitors and regulators can verify source data integrity without physical site visits, satisfying the data provenance requirements that make regulators hesitant to approve decentralized trial designs.

title: Instant music sync licensing
problem: A filmmaker, YouTuber, or advertiser who wants to license a song for their production must either navigate months-long negotiations with major labels — who often decline small requests entirely — or use generic royalty-free music, because there's no scalable way for independent artists to make their catalog licensable at standardized rates.
solutionSketch: A licensing registry where artists pre-set terms and prices for different use types — YouTube video, short film, TV ad, podcast — so any buyer can instantly purchase a sync license with automatic payment to all rights holders, without negotiation or a licensing intermediary.
whyEthereum: Enforcement: the license purchase and rights holder payment execute atomically in a single transaction — the buyer gets the license the moment they pay, and every co-writer and producer receives their split without a publishing administrator in the middle.

title: Decision markets for corporate governance
problem: Corporate decisions — which strategy to pursue, whether to hire or fire an executive, which product to prioritize — are made through a combination of politics, hierarchy, and intuition rather than mechanisms that aggregate genuine beliefs of those closest to the work. Board votes and management sign-off concentrate decision-making power in ways that reward confidence and seniority over accuracy, with no feedback loop that punishes bad predictions or rewards good ones. Organizations systematically act on what's good for those in power rather than what's good for the organization.
solutionSketch: Conditional prediction markets tied to company-specific metrics — share price, TVL, revenue, retention — where any proposal generates two parallel markets: expected metric outcome if it passes, and if it fails. The proposal executes if markets predict a positive impact. Participants with genuine information have financial incentive to trade accurately. Early implementations include Butter Markets (used in Optimism's grant allocation experiments) and MetaDAO, which has run 96+ proposals for 14 organizations using this mechanism.
whyEthereum: Enforcement: conditional markets execute and settle via smart contract, making the link between market signal and organizational decision a protocol property rather than management discretion. Composability: the same decision market infrastructure can be referenced by any organization's governance without rebuilding from scratch.

solutionSketch: A settlement layer for DER aggregation that meters individual device contributions, verifies demand reductions against smart meter baselines, and distributes compensation to device owners automatically — making it economically viable for aggregators to orchestrate millions of small assets into wholesale market participation.
whyEthereum: Enforcement: compensation for individual device contributions executes automatically when metered demand reductions are confirmed — enabling aggregators to settle millions of micro-transactions that would be uneconomic through traditional payment infrastructure.

whyEthereum: Verifiability: device actions and energy flow data are cryptographically logged — giving distribution operators an audit trail below the substation level that SCADA systems don't provide, and making unauthorized device commands forensically detectable.

whyEthereum: Composability: a shared settlement layer means any CPO-eMSP pair can transact without a pre-negotiated bilateral integration — roaming coverage expands from bilateral partnerships to the entire network by default.

title: Cross-jurisdictional fisheries quota tracking

title: Food provenance and traceability

title: Futarchy for public policy
problem: Democratic systems are good at aggregating what citizens want but systematically bad at determining which policies will actually deliver it. Voters choose representatives based on stated intentions; representatives vote on bills based on lobbying, ideology, and coalition politics rather than evidence of likely impact. Expert panels and think tanks aggregate some information but lack skin in the game — a consultant who recommends a bad policy faces no financial consequence.
solutionSketch: A governance layer that separates the question of values (decided democratically: what should we optimize for?) from the question of means (decided by markets: which policy will best achieve it?). Elected representatives define a measurable welfare metric — GDP, life expectancy, emissions index — and conditional prediction markets determine which policies are expected to raise it. A policy becomes law only when market estimates clearly predict it will improve welfare relative to the status quo. Robin Hanson's original formulation ('vote on values, bet on beliefs') has been live-tested by MetaDAO for DAO governance and explored by at least one government health agency since 2024.
whyEthereum: Enforcement: the link between market outcome and policy adoption executes automatically, removing the possibility of political override after the market has spoken. Verifiability: welfare metric measurement and market prices are publicly auditable, making it impossible to quietly override the market signal without detection.

title: Privacy-preserving firearms provenance for voluntary transfer verification

title: Hyperstition markets
problem: Many valuable outcomes — a new open standard getting adopted, a local currency achieving network effects, a civic technology deployed across a city — require enough people to act simultaneously that no individual will move first. solutionSketch: Markets designed not just to predict outcomes but to manifest them — where buying YES stakes participants financially in making a prediction true, and where public prices function as Schelling points that coordinate action around shared futures. whyEthereum: Composability: hyperstition markets can compose with attestation systems, identity layers, and impact certificates so that demonstrated contributions — not just financial bets — are verifiable and rewarded. title: Opportunity markets

whyEthereum: Enforcement: scout payouts execute automatically via smart contract when resolution conditions are met, removing the need for sponsors to manually evaluate and honor claims. solutionSketch: Parametric health benefit products where payouts trigger automatically when a standardized medical event is attested — hospital admission confirmed by the facility, specific ICD-10 diagnosis code recorded, preventive visit logged — executing payment within hours rather than weeks for claim types that don't require utilization review or medical necessity determination.
whyEthereum: Enforcement: payouts execute automatically when attested medical events match pre-defined trigger conditions — eliminating the manual claims process for product types where the trigger is binary and verifiable, while leaving complex claims to traditional adjudication.

title: Proof of personhood
problem: Any digital system that gives one vote, one reward, or one allocation per person is immediately gamed by whoever can spin up the most fake accounts — airdrops get drained by bots, governance votes get bought in bulk, and social platforms are flooded with coordinated inauthentic behavior — because there is no cheap, privacy-preserving way to prove an account belongs to a unique real human.
solutionSketch: Systems that establish a cryptographic guarantee that an account belongs to a unique living person — without revealing who that person is — enabling sybil-resistant token distributions, one-person-one-vote governance, and spam-free social platforms.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: personhood attestations are cryptographically issued and publicly checkable by any application — platforms verify uniqueness without storing biometric data or trusting a single identity provider that becomes a centralization point.

title: Public procurement lifecycle
problem: Government procurement processes are rife with opaque bid evaluations, paper-based contract trails, and limited public visibility, creating fertile ground for favoritism and corruption.
solutionSketch: Transparent record of tenders, bids, evaluations, awards, supplier credentials, deliveries, and payments spanning the full procurement cycle to reduce corruption and enable public audit
whyEthereum: Verifiability: the full procurement record — bids, evaluations, awards, and payments — is publicly auditable on a shared ledger, making favoritism and corruption detectable rather than just alleged.

title: Researcher credentials and peer review markets
problem: Academic recognition systems only reward first-author publications, leaving researchers who generate datasets, perform reviews, or replicate studies with no formal credit for work that is essential to science. Peer reviewers perform skilled labor for free on behalf of journals that charge institutions thousands per year — with reviews disappearing after use and no portable track record that follows the reviewer across journals.
solutionSketch: A market for peer review where journals post requests, qualified reviewers bid and are paid automatically on acceptance, and completed reviews become part of a portable verifiable track record — combined with credentials for dataset generation, replication work, and other non-publication contributions that carry the same weight as authorship.
whyEthereum: Composability: review contributions and payment history live on a shared layer readable by any institution or funding body — reviewers carry a verifiable track record across every journal they've worked with, not just those that maintain their own internal records.

title: Transparent carbon and biodiversity credit markets
problem: Carbon credits and biodiversity offsets are traded as undifferentiated commodities despite vast differences in methodology and verification rigor, allowing low-quality credits to crowd out legitimate ones. Forests, watersheds, and biodiversity also lack liquid market representations.
solutionSketch: Differentiated environmental asset classes with onchain provenance, methodology metadata, and verification quality — enabling transparent pricing of ecological assets and markets that reward genuine impact.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: provenance and methodology are cryptographically attached to each credit — buyers can verify quality without relying on opaque rating agencies, and double-counting is publicly detectable.

title: Research reagent and material provenance
problem: Scientific experiments that can't be replicated are often later traced to undisclosed variations in reagents, cell lines, or materials — a batch of antibodies that performed differently from what was published, a cell line that had been unknowingly contaminated — but there's no standard way to record or share the provenance of physical research materials that would let other labs understand what they're actually working with.
solutionSketch: Immutable provenance records for biological materials, reagents, and research tools — tracking origin, handling history, quality control results, and cross-references to experiments that used each lot — so that replication failures can be traced to their source.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: provenance records are cryptographically attested at each step of a material's lifecycle — a replication lab can independently verify they're working with the same reagent lot and handling conditions as the original study, rather than trusting self-reported descriptions.

title: Regenerative practice incentives

solutionSketch: Reward mechanisms that compensate farmers for sustainable and regenerative agricultural behaviors
whyEthereum: Verifiability: practice adoption and ecological outcomes can be attested on-chain using satellite imagery, IoT data, and third-party audits — creating a payment trail that funders can verify independently.

title: Migrant worker remittances
problem: A Kenyan nurse working in London sending $200 home loses $12–20 to Western Union and correspondent bank fees — more than the entire daily wage of the family member receiving it — while the transfer takes 1–3 days and requires both parties to have access to physical agents.
solutionSketch: Stablecoin transfers that move value internationally in minutes at near-zero marginal cost, with recipients cashing out through local mobile money networks or holding value in digital wallets without needing a bank account.
whyEthereum: Composability: stablecoins settle on a shared global layer without correspondent banking infrastructure — sender and recipient transact directly regardless of jurisdiction, with no intermediary banks extracting spread on each hop.

title: Verifiable dataset provenance and reuse tracking for research
problem: Researchers who create high-quality datasets — curating, cleaning, and annotating data that takes months of work — receive almost no academic credit when other researchers use their data, because there's no reliable mechanism to track dataset reuse across papers and institutions. Simultaneously, researchers who want to build on prior work often can't verify whether a dataset has been altered since publication or confirm they're working with the same version that produced the original findings.
solutionSketch: A registry where published datasets are cryptographically fingerprinted at the time of deposit, with every subsequent access and citation recorded — so dataset creators receive verifiable credit proportional to actual reuse, and downstream researchers can confirm they're working with an unaltered version of the original data.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: cryptographic fingerprints prove dataset integrity since publication, and onchain access records create an unfalsifiable citation trail — dataset creators get credit for actual reuse and downstream researchers can confirm data hasn't been tampered with.

whyEthereum: Enforcement: revenue flows are split and distributed automatically at the moment of receipt according to rules set once — no manual calculation, no payment delays, no disputes about the math.

whyEthereum: Enforcement: spending authorities and signing permissions are encoded in smart contracts and enforced programmatically — not dependent on each SaaS tool implementing policy correctly.

title: Smart-contract leasing

whyEthereum: Enforcement: rent payments, deposit holds, and renewal terms execute automatically via smart contract — neither party can unilaterally alter terms, and disputes resolve against pre-agreed code.

title: Automated royalty tracking and payments
problem: Royalty distribution in music, film, publishing, and patents passes through layers of opaque intermediaries who delay payments, misattribute rights, and make it nearly impossible for creators to audit what they're owed. Multi-party licensing agreements add further complexity — a single song can have dozens of co-writers, publishers, and performers each owed a different split, calculated manually and paid months after the usage occurred.
solutionSketch: Smart contracts that meter actual usage across media types and automatically distribute royalties to all rights holders at the moment of use — eliminating intermediary opacity, payment delays, and the manual calculation errors that compound across multi-party splits.
whyEthereum: Enforcement: usage is metered and payments execute automatically at the moment of use — rights holders receive what they're owed without relying on intermediaries to calculate or remit correctly.

title: Automated wills and estate execution
problem: Estate execution depends on manual probate processes that take months or years, while trust administration requires fiduciaries to manually manage distributions and reporting across jurisdictions, with beneficiaries having limited visibility.
solutionSketch: Time-locked, oracle-triggered estate execution and programmable trust administration with transparent record-keeping — assets transfer automatically when verifiable conditions are met.
whyEthereum: Enforcement: asset transfers execute automatically when death is confirmed via oracle — no probate court, no executor discretion, no months of delay.

title: Loyalty points as liquid, transferable assets

solutionSketch: Tokenized loyalty points that are transferable between programs, sellable on secondary markets, and governed by transparent, immutable issuance and expiry rules — so holders have real property rights over value they've earned.
whyEthereum: Composability: loyalty tokens on a shared layer are transferable between any programs that adopt the standard — points combine and flow across brands without bilateral partnership agreements between each issuer.

whyEthereum: Composability: tokenized policies trade on open markets and can be bundled, split, or collateralized — unlocking liquidity that paper policies permanently forfeit.

title: Real-time reserve attestation for insurance solvency
problem: Insurance regulators assess solvency through quarterly statutory filings that lag reality by months — in the interval between filings, an insurer's reserve position can deteriorate significantly without policyholders or regulators having visibility. The 2023 FIA surplus note controversy showed that even sophisticated state regulators can be caught off guard by rapid reserve changes between reporting periods.
solutionSketch: Onchain attestation of reserve assets that supplements existing statutory reporting — letting regulators and reinsurers see real-time reserve positions between quarterly filings, without replacing the existing RBC framework or requiring insurers to move actual reserve assets onto a blockchain.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: reserve attestations are cryptographically signed and continuously updated — regulators and reinsurers get intra-quarter visibility into reserve adequacy rather than waiting for the next statutory filing to detect deterioration.

title: Tokenized sovereign & municipal bonds
problem: Issuing and settling government debt involves layers of intermediaries, T+2 or longer settlement windows, and high minimum denominations that exclude smaller investors from participating.
solutionSketch: Onchain issuance, settlement, and coupon tracking of public debt instruments, enabling faster settlement, lower costs, and broader investor access
whyEthereum: Composability: tokenized bonds settle instantly, pay coupons automatically, and can be held directly by retail investors — removing intermediary layers and T+2 settlement delays.

title: Digital product passports
problem: The EU's Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) mandates digital product passports for most goods sold in Europe by 2030 — but no neutral infrastructure exists for brands, recyclers, and regulators across supply chains to read and write to a shared product record. Without it, origin and certification claims rely on paper trails that can be forged at every handoff, recycled materials lose their provenance once they re-enter supply chains, and secondhand buyers have no trustworthy way to verify repair history or remaining lifecycle value.
solutionSketch: Append-only product records that persist through every ownership transfer and material handoff — tracking origin, certifications, condition, repair history, and end-of-life status in a format any manufacturer, recycler, regulator, or secondhand buyer can read, satisfying ESPR requirements while making circular economy claims cryptographically verifiable rather than self-reported.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: every certification, ownership transfer, and material handoff is recorded as an immutable onchain event — fraud and greenwashing become publicly detectable, and the same product record is readable by any party in the supply chain without bilateral data-sharing agreements.

title: Transparent fund flows and disaster relief coordination
problem: Charitable donations, advocacy grants, and international aid flow through opaque intermediary chains where funds are lost to corruption, misallocation, or overhead — with donors unable to verify money reached its intended recipients. solutionSketch: Onchain tracking of fund flows from donor to final recipient with real-time visibility and audit logs — combined with shared coordination infrastructure for disaster response that lets all responding organizations see disbursements, supply distribution, and beneficiary verification in a single view.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: every fund transfer is recorded on a public ledger — donors can trace their contribution from receipt to final use without relying on the organization's own reporting.

title: Water rights trading and usage verification
problem: In drought-prone regions, water rights are traded in informal bilateral markets with no price transparency, while actual usage is monitored by infrequent physical inspections that miss illegal diversions — creating a tragedy of the commons where overuse is profitable and nearly undetectable until aquifers are depleted.
solutionSketch: Tokenized water rights tradeable on transparent markets, with IoT-verified usage continuously recorded onchain — creating a real-time allocation registry where overuse is immediately visible and rights can be transferred without paper title processes.
whyEthereum: Verifiability: actual water usage attested by IoT sensors is recorded immutably — illegal diversions become publicly detectable as deviations from onchain allocations, rather than discovered only when downstream users notice reduced flow.

problem: Wearable devices generate valuable biometric data that is locked inside proprietary platforms, giving individuals no way to share, monetize, or direct their own fitness and health information to researchers or insurers on their own terms.

whyEthereum: Composability: individuals connect their data to any research program or insurance product that accepts the standard — no platform lock-in, and users capture value from their own data.

whyEthereum: Verifiability: cryptographic timestamping on an immutable ledger proves exactly when evidence was recorded, making retroactive denial or tampering publicly detectable.

solutionSketch: Users prove claims from existing web platforms—income, identity, activity—for use in onchain applications, without requiring platform permission or surrendering raw data
whyEthereum: Verifiability: zero-knowledge proofs let users cryptographically attest to data from any website — income, identity, activity — without requiring platform permission or exposing underlying raw data.
